chunks: From them, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Hammad Abu Yusuf Al-Kazzaz, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Ali (peace be upon him) considered the paternal aunt to be in the position of the father in inheritance, and the maternal aunt to be in the position of the mother, and the son of the brother to be in the position of the brother.
He said: 'And every relative who is not entitled to a fixed share (fard) is in this same manner.'
He said: 'And Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: 'If there is an heir among those who have a fixed share, they are more entitled to the property.''
ai.seo_question: How does Imam Ali determine inheritance shares for aunts and uncles according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights Imam Ali’s (AS) juristic methodology of *qiyas* (analogical reasoning) in inheritance law, specifically equating the status of aunts and uncles to that of parents and siblings respectively. It establishes the principle that fixed-share heirs (*dhawu al-furud*) hold precedence over residuary heirs (*asaba*), a foundational concept in Shia fiqh for resolving complex inheritance scenarios. This approach underscores the rationality and consistency of the Ahl al-Bayt's legal interpretations in applying Quranic verses to extended family structures.
